newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER-PORTO EXTEND LEAD IN PORTUGUESE FIRST DIVISION.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PORTO EXTEND LEAD IN PORTUGUESE FIRST DIVISION.

text.p: Reigning champions Porto extended their lead in the Portuguese first division to four points with a 2-0 home win over Farense 2-0 on Sunday.
Porto, who beat Norway's Rosenborg 3-0 on Wednesday to reach the last eight of the European Cup, lead with 23 points although Benfica, in joint second place, are in action on Monday against Boavista.
Porto's Serbian playmaker Ljumbinko Drulovic set up the first goal with a cross in the 23rd minute which defender Jorge Costa headed in from close quarters.
After Brazilian striker Mario Jardel had hit Farense's left post in the 25th minute, he scored with a low shot from inside the box following a cross by compatriot Artur Oliveira in the 60th minute.

Ten minutes from the final whistle, Jardel lost a chance to score Porto's third goal when he hit the post with a penalty, awarded by the referee against Farense defender Acacio Fernandes for a foul on Oliveira.
A mistake by Belgian goalkeeper Filip De Wilde contributed to Sporting Lisbon's 1-0 defeat away against Braga on Saturday, the second blow for the team within a week.
Sporting, eliminated from the UEFA Cup by France's Metz on Tuesday, played the last half hour with 10 men after captain Oceano Cruz was sent off for two bookable offences.
Four minutes from the end, De Wilde left the box late to try to intercept a free-kick by midfielder Luis Baltasar, but striker Antonio Duarte got to the ball first and headed it into a deserted net.
